title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Problem I (§XXIII) is the first of Euler's systematic list of end-condition cases for the transverse vibration of an elastic lamina, announced in §XXII. Here the lamina is completely free (or lies on a horizontal plane).

Set-up:
- The lamina has length a; length k of it weighs K.
- The elastic moment for curvature radius r is Kcc/r, which in modern terms means EI corresponds to K·cc.
- With Euler's time unit (2h being his gravity constant in his units of time), he sets b^4 = 2hk·cc.
- cc is taken from the static deflection experiment described earlier: cc = (1/3)·I·k^3/(iK), the cantilever end-load formula δ = PL^3/(3EI). Hence b^4 = (2/3)·I h k^4/(iK).
- The small deflection y(x,t) obeys Euler-Bernoulli beam dynamics, written as y_tt = b^4 y_xxxx.

Separated (normal-mode) solution:
y = cos(θ²t)·[A cos u + B sin u + C e^u + D e^{-u}], with u = θx/b.

Boundary conditions at the free end F (x = 0):
- No force and no moment, so y'' = 0 and y''' = 0.
- Since y'' ∝ −A cos u − B sin u + C e^u + D e^{-u}, y'' = 0 at x = 0 gives A = C + D.
- Since y''' ∝ A sin u − B cos u + C e^u − D e^{-u}, y''' = 0 at x = 0 gives B = C − D.

Continuation on the next page:
- The same two conditions are imposed at x = a, writing ζ = θa/b.
- Eliminating the constants gives the free-free frequency equation cos ζ · cosh ζ = 1, written as 2 = cos ζ (e^ζ + e^{-ζ}).
- Its roots are ζ ≈ 4.730, 7.853, ... plus the trivial ζ = 0 (the rigid/rest state).
- The frequency is θ² = ζ²b²/a².

The page thus serves the classification of vibration species of free, pinned and clamped laminae.
errors: Sign slip: with the time factor cos(θ²t) one has y_tt = −θ^4 y, while b^4 y_xxxx = +θ^4 y for the stated spatial function. The printed equation (ddy/dt²) = b^4(d^4y/dx^4) should carry a minus sign (y_tt = −b^4 y_xxxx), or else the trial solution does not satisfy it. The error is harmless for the eigenvalue analysis.
Labeling inconsistency: the text names the lamina AB (with AX = x) but refers to the free extremity as F (and on the next page G), following the letters of Fig. 4 rather than the letters of the text.

ideas.what: Separated normal-mode solution of the beam equation with trigonometric and exponential (hyperbolic) spatial parts
ideas.where_published: E65 Additamentum I (1744), E40/E126 era papers, and this paper E443

ideas.what: Free-end conditions y'' = y''' = 0 (vanishing moment and shear) imposed at the end x = 0
ideas.modern_name: Free boundary conditions for a beam

ideas.what: Calibration of the flexural rigidity (Kcc) from a static cantilever deflection experiment, cc = I k^3/(3iK)
ideas.modern_name: Static measurement of EI via the cantilever deflection formula PL^3/(3EI)
ideas.where_published: Earlier sections of E443; cf. E65

ideas.what: Free-free beam frequency equation cos ζ cosh ζ = 1 (derived on the following page from the conditions set up here)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli (1742) and Euler; systematic six-case treatment Euler E443, as discussed by Truesdell 1960
ideas.where_published: E443 (Novi Comm. Petrop. 17); Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (1960)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard, well-documented setup of the free-free beam vibration problem. Euler's six-case classification in E443 is covered in Truesdell's history; nothing on this page appears absent from the literature beyond a minor sign slip.
transcription_corrections: 'cc = \frac{1}{2}\frac{I.k^3}{iK}' should read cc = \frac{1}{3}\frac{I.k^3}{iK} (consistent with the cantilever formula and with b^4 = 2hk·cc).
'b^4 = \frac{2}{2}\frac{I\,b.k^4}{iK} [?]' should read b^4 = \frac{2}{3}\frac{I\,h.k^4}{iK} (h, not b; factor 2/3).
Marginal note 'Tab. VII. Fig. 4.' is correctly read.
